import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def _norm_sku(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return None
    return str(x).strip().upper()


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    orders = inputs["orders"].copy()
    price_list = inputs["price_list"].copy()

    # ---- expression: sku_norm ----
    orders["sku_norm"] = orders["sku"].apply(_norm_sku)

    # keep track of original row order/index
    orders = orders.reset_index(drop=True)
    orders["_orig_idx"] = orders.index

    # normalize price_list sku for join
    price_list = price_list.copy()
    price_list["_sku_norm_price"] = price_list["sku"].apply(_norm_sku)

    # ---- lookup ----
    # only rows with non-null sku_norm can possibly match
    orders_for_join = orders[orders["sku_norm"].notna()]

    merged = orders_for_join.merge(
        price_list,
        left_on="sku_norm",
        right_on="_sku_norm_price",
        how="inner",
        suffixes=("_ord", "_price"),
    )

    # apply condition: price_list.valid_from <= order_date
    if not merged.empty:
        cond = merged["valid_from"] <= merged["order_date"]
        merged = merged[cond]

    if not merged.empty:
        # tie-break: greatest valid_from, then lowest list_id
        merged_sorted = merged.sort_values(
            by=["_orig_idx", "valid_from", "list_id"],
            ascending=[True, False, True],
        )
        best = merged_sorted.groupby("_orig_idx", as_index=True).first()
    else:
        best = pd.DataFrame(columns=merged.columns).set_index(
            pd.Index([], name="_orig_idx")
        )

    # build unit_price / price_flag aligned to original orders
    unit_price = pd.Series(np.nan, index=orders["_orig_idx"], dtype="float64")
    price_flag = pd.Series("NO_PRICE", index=orders["_orig_idx"], dtype="object")

    if not best.empty:
        unit_price.loc[best.index] = best["unit_price"].astype(float).values
        price_flag.loc[best.index] = "OK"

    # rows with no match (including NULL sku_norm) get unit_price = 0
    unit_price = unit_price.fillna(0.0)

    orders = orders.set_index("_orig_idx")
    orders["unit_price"] = unit_price
    orders["price_flag"] = price_flag
    orders = orders.reset_index(drop=True)

    # ---- expression: ext_amount ----
    def _ext(row):
        if pd.isna(row["qty"]):
            return np.nan
        return row["qty"] * row["unit_price"]

    orders["ext_amount"] = orders.apply(_ext, axis=1)

    # ---- router ----
    def _route(row):
        qty = row["qty"]
        price_flag = row["price_flag"]
        ext_amount = row["ext_amount"]

        # Rule 1: REVIEW
        cond1 = False
        if price_flag == "NO_PRICE":
            cond1 = True
        elif pd.isna(qty):
            cond1 = True
        elif qty >= 100:
            cond1 = True
        if cond1:
            return "REVIEW"

        # Rule 2: BULK
        if not pd.isna(ext_amount) and ext_amount >= 1000:
            return "BULK"

        # Rule 3: SMALL
        if not pd.isna(ext_amount) and ext_amount < 50:
            return "SMALL"

        return "STANDARD"

    orders["route"] = orders.apply(_route, axis=1)

    # ---- output 1: order_enriched ----
    order_enriched = orders[["order_id", "sku_norm", "unit_price", "route"]].copy()

    # ---- aggregator ----
    grouped = orders.groupby(["route", "order_date"], dropna=False)
    order_count = grouped.size().reset_index(name="order_count")
    total_ext = grouped["ext_amount"].sum(min_count=0).reset_index(name="total_ext")
    # sum() with skipna default ignores NaNs; all-NaN group yields 0.0 already
    total_ext["total_ext"] = total_ext["total_ext"].fillna(0.0)

    route_daily = order_count.merge(total_ext, on=["route", "order_date"], how="left")
    route_daily = route_daily[["route", "order_date", "order_count", "total_ext"]]
